11.t: Working with data: a heating curve
q: At what temperature did the ice melt?
For how many minutes did the temperature stay at 0 degrees C?
From about 1 to 4 minutes: about 3 minutes.
Describe what happened between 12 and 14 minutes and what the water was doing.
The temperature stayed at 100 degrees C: the water was boiling, changing to a gas.
Explain why the temperature stops rising during melting and boiling even though the hot plate is still on.

The energy from the hot plate is used to free the particles from each other (break the attractions) and change the state, not to make them move faster, so the temperature stays the same until the change is complete.
